clue.text: Lean the wrong way, drop a catch

indicators.note: going the wrong way means the word for lean is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: to tip is to lean or tilt
a drop or plunge is a fall

explanation.surface: A fielder overbalances and spills an easy catch in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop a catch' reads as cricket fumbling, but 'catch' is the definition, in its sense of a hidden snag.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden danger or snag, which is what a catch means in phrases like 'what's the catch?'

clue.text: Skip page, dream time away

indicators.note: away means removed, so that letter is taken out of the dream word

blocks.note: p is the standard abbreviation for page
a trance is a dreamlike state
t is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone skips a page and daydreams the time away.
explanation.definitionFit: To prance is to move with lively springing steps, which is how a person skips about.

clue.text: Romeo trapped by title, sick at heart, like Hamlet

indicators.note: something trapped by another is held inside it
the heart of a word is its centre, so only its middle letters are kept

blocks.note: a tag is a label or title
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet
the two central letters of sick

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's Romeo, lovesick and trapped by his name, resembles Hamlet.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Hamlet suggest a Shakespeare pairing, but Romeo is only a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is a tragedy, so describing something as being like that play means it is a tragedy in kind.

clue.text: Give notice to cleric

blocks.note: an ad is a notice in a paper
a minister is a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: Someone hands formal notice to a priest.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to dispense or apply, as with medicine or punishment, so it means to give out.

clue.text: Grand room providing storage above yard

indicators.note: in a down entry, above means the room word is placed before the yard piece

blocks.note: a loft is the roof-space room used for storing things
y is the abbreviation for yard

explanation.surface: An imposing attic room offers storage over the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Lofty means elevated or noble in bearing, the same sense as grand or stately.

clue.text: To drink without company proved a disaster

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the drinking word wraps round the other

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in sips
a crew is a company of workers, as on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone drinking alone found it ended badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without company' looks like 'alone', but 'without' means outside, and 'company' is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw-up is colloquial for a botched job or fiasco, the same thing as a disaster in casual speech.

clue.text: Barred item at work time, creating TV drama

blocks.note: soap is commonly sold in bars
op, short for opus, is a work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Something banned at the workplace causes a dramatic scene for television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barred' suggests banned, but it means sold in bar form.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a long-running serial television programme about everyday lives, a kind of TV drama.

clue.text: Rubbish a job listing

blocks.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses an advert for a vacancy as rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job listing' suggests a vacancy advert, but it is a list of who does which job when.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule showing the order in which people take turns at duties.

clue.text: Retro tie with decoration, seen on front row outfits

indicators.note: retro means backwards, so the word for tie is read in reverse
the front of a word is its first letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a tie in a match is a draw
the opening letter of row
the OBE, Order of the British Empire, is an honour

explanation.surface: A vintage tie with a pattern is worn by people in the front row of a fashion show.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch, often called a decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a person's entire collection of clothes, the sum of their outfits.

clue.text: Family secure involvement of detective and free missing female

indicators.note: involvement means taking something in, so the secure word wraps round the detective
missing means lacking, so the letter for female is dropped from the free word

blocks.note: to peg is to fix or secure
DI is a detective inspector
taken as written
f is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A family tries to get a detective involved to free a missing woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedigree means ancestry or lineage, a recorded line of descent, which is one sense of family.

clue.text: A large branch gets a wake-up call

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
an arm is a branch, as of a river or an organisation

explanation.surface: A big department of a company receives a rude awakening.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarm is the bell or clock signal that rouses a sleeper, literally a call to get up.

clue.text: Complimented little chap drinking coffee

indicators.note: someone drinking takes the drink inside, so the chap's name surrounds the coffee

blocks.note: Fred is a short man's name, the diminutive of Frederick
a latte is a milky coffee

explanation.surface: A small man sipping his coffee receives praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To be flattered is to have been praised, often excessively, matching complimented as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Domestic tip for a more effective stack

definitions.text: Domestic tip for a more effective stack

blocks.clueFragment: Domestic tip for a more effective stack
blocks.note: surface reading: a household hint for piling things up more efficiently
setter's reading: the topmost fitting of a house's smoke stack, which improves the draw

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' reads as advice, but it means the very top; a stack is the brick column on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney pot is the earthenware pipe fitted to the top of a chimney stack on a house, improving its draught.

clue.text: Fastening for jumper

blocks.note: first meaning: an ornamental braided loop-and-button closure on a coat
second meaning: an amphibian that leaps

explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests the British word for a sweater, so a fastening for one sounds like a button; here it is an animal that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a decorative coat fastening of braid and a leaping amphibian.

clue.text: People there wreck a tent at ball

indicators.note: wrecking something leaves it in pieces, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Revellers at a dance destroy a marquee.
explanation.definitionFit: Attendance means the people present at an event, the crowd who are there.

clue.text: Predisposed to subtle spice blend

indicators.note: a blend mixes ingredients together, so the letters are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: the eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone has a liking for a delicately flavoured spice mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Being susceptible means being liable or prone to something, the same sense as predisposed.

clue.text: One can work things out using this playground equipment control

definitions.text: One can work things out using this

blocks.note: a slide is a playground chute
to rule is to control

explanation.surface: A child figures out how to work the playground slide.
explanation.definitionFit: A slide rule is a mechanical calculating instrument with sliding logarithmic scales, used for working sums out.

clue.text: Bill about to divide ballot for lawyer

indicators.note: something that divides another sits in its middle, splitting it into two parts

blocks.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement, an ad
a ballot is a vote
ca, circa, means about

explanation.surface: A proposed law is set to split the electorate over a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a proposed law or a man's name, but it is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: An advocate is a person who pleads a case in court, especially in Scotland, so a lawyer.

clue.text: With no one around, I planned to eat nothing

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so the planned word swallows the nothing

blocks.note: taken as written
something slated is scheduled or planned
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Alone, I decided to eat nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The picture of solitary fasting hides that 'planned' gives one word with nothing put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolated describes being cut off and solitary, the condition of having nobody nearby.

clue.text: Having missed out at home, tucked into spread

indicators.note: out here means disordered, so the letters of the preceding word are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
someone at home is in
to tuck into food is to eat it, past tense

explanation.surface: Someone who missed going out stayed home and ate a big spread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a meal being tucked into, but it is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To disseminate is to scatter or broadcast widely, as with news or seeds, the verb sense of spread.

clue.text: Student in scrap with man is completely unconcerned

indicators.note: in places the student letter inside the scrap word

blocks.note: a scrap is a small bit
L is a learner, as on British learner-driver plates
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: A student in a fight with a man shows no worry at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests a fight, but it means a fragment.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means carefree and casually indifferent, showing a total lack of worry or care.

clue.text: Tails partner to slippery path

indicators.note: something slippery slides about, so these letters move out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dog's companion wags along an icy path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tails' suggests animals or a coin; here it is the formal tailcoat, which is worn with a tall hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A top hat is the tall silk hat traditionally worn with a tailcoat, so it partners tails in formal dress.

clue.text: Struggles to take top off paint

indicators.note: removing the top of a word means its first letter is dropped

blocks.note: toils are hard struggles or labours

explanation.surface: Someone battles to get the lid off a tin of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils are oil-based artists' colours, so the plural noun is a kind of paint used on canvas.

clue.text: Slip quantity into vegetable and herb with duck

indicators.note: putting something into another means it sits inside the vegetable word

blocks.note: a pea is a vegetable
cc, cubic centimetres, measures a quantity of liquid
dill is a feathery herb
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter that looks like zero

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction to add a measure of something to vegetables, herbs and duck.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen picture hides that 'Slip' is the definition, a small fault rather than a cooking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a minor sin or trivial wrongdoing, which a slip, a small lapse or error, also names.

clue.text: Belief in honour? Leave it out, love!

indicators.note: leave it out tells you to omit the word it, here part of the instruction itself

blocks.note: credit is honour or acknowledgement
love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O

explanation.surface: Someone protests a claim about honour with the slang 'Leave it out, love!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave it out' is British slang for 'stop it', but here it literally removes the letters IT from CREDIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A credo is a statement of faith or guiding principles, the Latin for 'I believe', so a belief.

clue.text: Pass through without first stopping

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the through word sits round the chosen letter
first picks out only the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: via means by way of, through
the opening letter of stopping

explanation.surface: A traveller goes straight through a country without first making a stop.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is an official permit allowing entry to a country, a kind of pass.

clue.text: Said thank you in turn, joining praise for property

indicators.note: turning the word round means its letters are read from end to start
joining says the next piece is simply attached after the first

blocks.note: ta is what Britons say informally for thank you
a tribute is an act or words of praise

explanation.surface: Guests take turns thanking and praising someone at a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks; 'said' signals it is a spoken word.
explanation.definitionFit: An attribute is a quality or characteristic, which is the abstract sense of a property, as in a property of copper.

clue.text: Level score

blocks.note: first meaning: a step or degree
second meaning: to achieve or chalk up, or a nick cut as a tally mark

explanation.walkthrough: Read together, the clue sounds like a tied match; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a degree on a scale and a cut tally mark, or as a verb to achieve a win.

clue.text: Willing to finish first — it's nearly over now

indicators.note: first places the finishing word before the willing word rather than after it

blocks.note: a finish is an end
someone game is willing to have a go

explanation.surface: A keen competitor wants to win while the contest is almost done.
explanation.definitionFit: The endgame is the final phase of a chess match or other contest, the stage when things are almost finished.

clue.text: Hard left get too excited, then get stuffed

indicators.note: left in the sense of departed, so that letter goes away from the word

blocks.note: to overheat is figuratively to get too worked up
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: An extremist of the hard left loses their temper and is told rudely to go away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard left' reads as politics and 'get stuffed' as an insult; in fact one letter departs and the definition is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: To overeat is to consume too much food, so you literally become stuffed full.
